raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`/rerun-test` and `/rerun-group` edit their reply comment as the run progresses (⏳ → 🔄 → ✅/❌), so the PR conversation shows whether the tests passed. `/run-cpu-ci` (#45501) only posts a one-time `🚀 Running base-a-test-cpu …` comment and never updates it. Its run is a `workflow_dispatch` on `main`, so it doesn't appear in the PR's checks either. The only way to see the result is to open the run link (example: #47063).

## Modifications

- `slash_command_handler.py` (`handle_run_cpu_ci`): post the reply comment **before** dispatching, then pass `reply_comment_id` and `reply_marker` (`<!--rrt:0-->`) as dispatch inputs. Afterwards, edit that same comment to show the run link, with `⏳` and the marker at the end of the line. A dispatch failure is written into the same comment.
- `run-cpu-ci.yml`: add the two inputs and a `write-back-result` job (`needs: base-a-test-cpu`, `if: always()`). It runs the existing `update_rerun_test_status.py` to set ✅ when the stage succeeds and ❌ otherwise, mirroring `rerun-test.yml`.
- Security model unchanged: the workflow-level token stays read-only, so the stage running PR code still has no write access. Only the separate writeback job gets `issues`/`pull-requests: write`, and it checks out `main` (the dispatch ref), not the PR.
- Docs: one line each in `contribution_guide.mdx` and the `ci-workflow-guide` skill.

There's no 🔄 "runner picked up" beacon: adding it would mean editing `_pr-test-stage-cpu.yml`, which PR CI shares. The comment goes straight from ⏳ to ✅/❌. A run cancelled by a re-dispatch on the same SHA is marked ❌. The new dispatch has its own comment.

## Testing

- Mock run of `handle_run_cpu_ci` with run-URL lookup both succeeding and failing. Checked the dispatch inputs and the comment body, then fed that body through `update_rerun_test_status.main()` for both success and failure: the line flips to ✅/❌ and the marker becomes `<!--rrt:0:done-->`.
- `ruff format --check` (0.15.1) passes. The YAML parses (jobs `check-changes`, `base-a-test-cpu`, `write-back-result`).
- Not yet exercised end to end: the slash-command handler and `run-cpu-ci.yml` both run from `main`, so this takes effect only after merge. Verify with a `/run-cpu-ci` on any PR then.

@@ -405,7 +405,7 @@ group: pr-test-{event_name}-{branch}-{pr_sha}-{stage}
 | `/run-extra-ci amd`, `/run-amd-extra-ci`, `/run-ci amd-extra` | Adds `run-ci` and `run-ci-amd-extra`, then reruns only AMD Extra, including green runs. Base CI behavior is unchanged; existing labels are kept. |
 | `/rerun-test <test-file> [<test-file> ...]` | Reruns specific test file(s) via `rerun-test.yml`. A file arg containing a glob metacharacter (`*`, `?`, `[...]`) expands against `test/registered/` and the multimodal test dir to every matching `test_*.py` (e.g. `/rerun-test test_*backend*.py` — wrap in backticks so GitHub doesn't italicize the `*`); matches are deduped, grouped by dispatch shape, and can't carry a `::test` selector. No match → single ⛔ reply, nothing dispatched. |
 | `/rerun-group <group> [<group> ...]` | Expands registered test groups, then reuses `/rerun-test` |
-| `/run-cpu-ci` | Dispatches `run-cpu-ci.yml` on main: only the `base-a-test-cpu` suite, at the PR head SHA, no caches saved. Same gate as `/rerun-test`. Alias: `/rerun-cpu-ci` |
+| `/run-cpu-ci` | Dispatches `run-cpu-ci.yml` on main: only the `base-a-test-cpu` suite, at the PR head SHA, no caches saved; writes ✅/❌ back to its reply comment. Same gate as `/rerun-test`. Alias: `/rerun-cpu-ci` |
 
 Handled by `scripts/ci/utils/slash_command_handler.py` → `.github/workflows/slash-command-handler.yml`.

@@ -6,6 +6,8 @@
 # workflow it calls are trusted; only the code under test comes from the PR.
 # That code runs on hosted runners with a read-only token and no secrets
 # (nothing here inherits them), the same exposure as `/rerun-test` cpu mode.
+# The pass/fail result is written back to the handler's reply comment by a
+# separate job that checks out main, as rerun-test.yml does.
 name: Run CPU CI
 run-name: "[run-cpu-ci] ${{ inputs.git_ref }}"
 
@@ -35,6 +37,18 @@ on:
         required: false
         type: boolean
         default: true
+      # Set by the slash-command handler: the reply comment write-back-result
+      # updates with ✅/❌, and the marker locating its line.
+      reply_comment_id:
+        description: "Reply comment ID to write back result to"
+        required: false
+        type: string
+        default: ""
+      reply_marker:
+        description: "Marker for locating the line in the reply comment"
+        required: false
+        type: string
+        default: ""
 
 concurrency:
   group: run-cpu-ci-${{ inputs.git_ref }}
@@ -67,3 +81,36 @@ jobs:
       caller_inputs: ${{ toJson(inputs) }}
       partitions: ${{ needs.check-changes.outputs.partitions }}
       run_timeout_minutes: '15'
+
+  # Its own job, so the stage keeps the read-only token: only this job, which
+  # runs main's code and no PR code, can write to the PR's comments.
+  write-back-result:
+    needs: base-a-test-cpu
+    if: always() && inputs.reply_comment_id != '' && inputs.reply_marker != ''
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    permissions:
+      issues: write
+      pull-requests: write
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout code
+        uses: actions/checkout@v4
+
+      - name: Set up Python
+        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: '3.12'
+
+      - name: Write back result to reply comment
+        env:
+          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+        run: |
+          if [[ "${{ needs.base-a-test-cpu.result }}" == "success" ]]; then
+            STATUS=success
+          else
+            STATUS=failure
+          fi
+          python3 scripts/ci/utils/update_rerun_test_status.py \
+            --comment-id "${{ inputs.reply_comment_id }}" \
+            --marker "${{ inputs.reply_marker }}" \
+            --status "$STATUS" \
+            --repo "${{ github.repository }}"

@@ -154,7 +154,7 @@ For CI to run on a pull request, it must have the "run-ci" label. Authorized use
 - `/run-extra-ci amd` (also `/run-amd-extra-ci`, `/run-ci amd-extra`): Adds "run-ci" and "run-ci-amd-extra", then reruns only AMD Extra. Both hardware Extra commands include successful runs and also accept `/rerun-extra-ci <hardware>`.
 - `/rerun-test <test-spec> [<test-spec> ...]`: Reruns one or more specific tests directly. A spec may select a file, class, or method using `<file>::<TestClass>[.<test_method>]`. Multiple specs and file globs are supported. `--changed` (short form `-c`) adds every test file the PR itself adds or modifies (under `test/registered/` or the multimodal test directory), so a PR that touches several tests can rerun them all without listing them. Examples: `/rerun-test test_srt_endpoint.py`, `/rerun-test registered/core/test_srt_endpoint.py::TestSRTEndpoint.test_simple_decode`, `/rerun-test test_a.py test_b.py`, `/rerun-test test_*backend*.py`, `/rerun-test --changed`, or `/rerun-test -c`.
 - `/rerun-group <group> [<group> ...]`: Expands one or more registered test groups (for example, `/rerun-group rust-server`) and dispatches their tests through the same selective-rerun workflow. Groups are defined in [`scripts/ci/rerun_test_groups.json`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/scripts/ci/rerun_test_groups.json).
-- `/run-cpu-ci`: Runs only the CPU unit suite (`base-a-test-cpu`) against the PR head, partitioned the same way as in PR CI, without the `run-ci` label or any GPU stage. For a small PR, `/run-cpu-ci` plus `/rerun-group <module>` covers the unit tests and the affected module's tests. Alias: `/rerun-cpu-ci`.
+- `/run-cpu-ci`: Runs only the CPU unit suite (`base-a-test-cpu`) against the PR head, partitioned the same way as in PR CI, without the `run-ci` label or any GPU stage. Its reply comment turns ✅/❌ when the run finishes, as `/rerun-test` does. For a small PR, `/run-cpu-ci` plus `/rerun-group <module>` covers the unit tests and the affected module's tests. Alias: `/rerun-cpu-ci`.
 
 The no-argument Base aliases share the existing multi-hardware retry scope; they do not opt every hardware tier in. Existing gates still apply. `/run-ci <tier>` selects only that tier, while legacy `/tag-and-rerun-ci <tier>` adds labels and retries broadly. Unknown or multiple arguments to `/run-ci` are rejected.

@@ -1729,6 +1729,9 @@ def handle_run_cpu_ci(gh_repo, pr, comment, user_perms, token):
     Always dispatched on main with the head SHA as an input, for forks and
     in-repo PRs alike, so the workflow definition is main's. It runs PR code on
     hosted runners with no secrets, so it takes the /rerun-test gate.
+
+    Like /rerun-test, the reply comment is posted before dispatching so the run
+    can write its result back to it (update_rerun_test_status.py).
     """
     if not _check_rerun_test_permissions(
         gh_repo, pr, comment, user_perms, "run-cpu-ci"
@@ -1750,12 +1753,21 @@ def handle_run_cpu_ci(gh_repo, pr, comment, user_perms, token):

@@ -1765,7 +1777,7 @@ def handle_run_cpu_ci(gh_repo, pr, comment, user_perms, token):
